# Roadmap — evidence-intake-project

Live milestones in `after` order, then standing tracks. Acceptance verdicts are computed
from evidence under the descendant-commit rule (D-016).

## Milestones

### Case assembly: the missing middle between extraction and digest

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.assembly.case-assembly/1`

Build the layer the external review found missing: reviewed, append-only semantic interpretation over immutable content; descriptive provenance edges and lineage; occurrence candidates; proposition packets as the primary workspace; and a deterministic, template-rendered, source-linked layered digest. The binding constraint is manual entry: most semantic fields cannot be detected without a language model, which the project declines, so the enrichment workflow is designed around a measured keystroke budget (inherit from a source profile, sweep one field across passages, one key to accept or refuse a deterministic candidate). No scoring, no merging, no occurrence or independence declared by a machine. The full plan is docs/case-assembly-plan.md.

### Office layer foundation: clients, matters, calendar, and the Court/Office workspace

`completed` · `@evidence-intake-project.office.court-office-foundation/1`

Wrap the evidence kernel in the first slice of the public-defender office layer: an office-core crate with its own store (users, clients, matters, assignments, courts, appearances, deadlines, notes), the optional matter-to-evidence-case link, office-wide search with conservative conflict prompts, and the WinSafe GUI reorganized into a calendar-first Court pane and an Office pane hosting the existing intake and review surfaces. Corresponds to CMS-0 plus the calendar/docket core of CMS-1 in docs/office-layer-plan.md; reporting builder, custom fields, timekeeping, multi-user server, PWA and communications are later milestones.

> **Note:** Local-first, single-machine, SQLite. Schema written for eventual PostgreSQL portability behind evidence-server, but no server, RBAC or sync in this milestone. GUI work happens in Windows sessions; schema, stores, read models and CLI are buildable on Linux.
